title: Composite error taxonomy and pager-policy synthesizer for SLO-driven alerting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable 'Composite Error Taxonomy' and a Pager Policy Synthesizer that combine tracing hooks, enriched metric/log signals, and SLO burn-rate analysis to produce contextualized alerts and suggested paging actions. Goal is to reduce noisy oncall wakeups by 35% while improving time-to-detection for high-impact regressions. This ticket spans: trace enrichment, metric/log pipeline tagging, anomaly scoring, and a lightweight decision engine that proposes pager routing (oncall, silent, ticket) with rationale and links to linked traces and top contributing spans.
acceptance_criteria: Composite taxonomy defined and stored in a config-driven format (service, symptom, likely-cause categories)
Tracing instrumentation emits taxonomy tags via a small enrichment hook (trace attribute keys documented)
Metrics/log pipeline attaches taxonomy labels and anomaly score to relevant events in ingestion layer
Alert decision engine uses SLO burn-rate + taxonomy + anomaly score to generate a suggested paging action for each alert
Suggested paging actions surfaced in alert payload and in Console alert debug view with links to top traces and a one-line rationale
Reduction in median noisy pages in staging alert stream by >= 25% with no increase in missed-high-impact incidents (validated by manual review)
technical_notes: Taxonomy format: YAML document with service namespaces, symptom enums (latency, error-class, resource-saturation), and cause-score weights

Trace enrichment hook will be implemented as lightweight patch in runtime tracing library (non-blocking, best-effort), emits attributes: rwi.taxonomy.symptom, rwi.taxonomy.cause_hint, rwi.anomaly.score

Anomaly scoring uses a hybrid signal: short-window z-score on latency percentiles + error-rate spike detector + histogram skew. We will prototype with existing streaming infra (Kafka -> Flink job) to attach scores before metric ingestion

Decision engine is rules-first with fallback ML scorer: rules include burn-rate thresholds, taxonomy severity mapping, and service SLA tier. ML scorer is a simple logistic model used only to rank-page vs ticket when rules ambiguous
Backwards compatibility: if taxonomy labels are missing, system falls back to current burn-rate-only alerting behaviour
Privacy: taxonomy labels are non-sensitive, no customer payloads are included. Audit trail for decisions persisted in alerts-index for 30d
tasks: Design taxonomy schema and review with SRE/Oncall leads (owner: Maya)
Implement trace enrichment hook and unit tests (owner: Eng-team-tracing)
Add enrichment stage to metrics/log pipeline; prototype in staging (owner: Observability-pipeline)
Build decision engine service (rules + ML scorer) and endpoint to return suggested action
Wire suggested action into existing alert router and Console alert payload
Run 2-week canary on non-production alert stream, collect signal: noisy pages, time-to-detect, false-positive rate
Document runbook updates and create rollback plan
